idiom_name: uniform stage contract + explicit pipe/queue connectors + one assembly root
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one record type (or stream chunk type) that every stage consumes and produces, express each filter as a callable with the shape stage(inbound) -> outbound that iterates lazily and emits as it goes, and make the pipe an explicit connector object (queue, channel, stream, channel pair) that owns buffering and backpressure rather than letting stages call each other directly. Compose the stages in a single assembly step so order and error policy live in one place, keep filters free of construction and transport details, and pick the pipe implementation last: in-process iterators for pure transformations, queues or OS pipes once stages must overlap, processes or brokers once they must be isolated or scaled separately. The classic Filter/Pipe classes are only justified when stages are configured, monitored or deployed at runtime; otherwise a plain function chain realises the same pattern more cheaply.
code_sketch:
records = source()                       # Data Source
for stage in [normalise, validate, enrich, redact]:   # Filters
    records = stage(records)             # each returns a lazy stream
for record in records:                   # Data Sink
    sink.write(record)
pitfalls: Letting a filter call the next filter directly: the chain is then hard-wired, cannot be reordered and cannot be distributed.
Unbounded buffering between stages, presented as decoupling: latency and memory grow without limit because nothing applies backpressure.
Hidden shared state (caches, buffers, counters) inside a filter, which silently breaks reordering, retries and parallel instances.

Wrong move: let each filter emit a different undocumented payload shape -> downstream filters fail at runtime or silently misread fields -> instead version and validate the record contract at every pipe boundary.

Wrong move: acknowledge a record when an intermediate filter enqueues it -> a crash before the sink commits causes loss or ambiguous redelivery -> instead acknowledge only after durable sink completion and make retries idempotent.

Wrong move: parallelise an order-sensitive stage without carrying sequence keys -> output order changes and downstream state becomes incorrect -> instead partition by key, preserve sequence metadata, or keep that stage ordered.
